Joint BART models for responses with non-ignorable missingness

Source: R/samplers.R
missBART.Rd

missBART1() and missBART2() fit the two selection models of Goh, Soh, Parnell and Murphy (2024). Both use multivariate BART for the responses. missBART1() models the missingness indicators with a multivariate probit regression on (1, x, y); missBART2() uses a multivariate probit BART model on (x, y). Missing responses are imputed within the sampler. missBARTprobit() is the former name of missBART1().

Usage

missBART1(
  x,
  y,
  x_predict = NULL,
  n_trees = 100,
  burn = 1000,
  iters = 1000,
  thin = 2,
  predict = TRUE,
  tree_prior_params = tree_list(...),
  hypers = hypers_list(...),
  scale = TRUE,
  include_x = TRUE,
  include_y = TRUE,
  show_progress = TRUE,
  progress_every = 10,
  pdp_range = c(-0.5, 0.5),
  make_pdp = FALSE,
  mice_impute = TRUE,
  ymis_update = c("conditional", "marginal"),
  probit_prior = probit_prior_list(),
  save_y_pred = TRUE,
  save_z = TRUE,
  ...
)

missBARTprobit(
  x,
  y,
  x_predict = NULL,
  n_trees = 100,
  burn = 1000,
  iters = 1000,
  thin = 2,
  predict = TRUE,
  tree_prior_params = tree_list(...),
  hypers = hypers_list(...),
  scale = TRUE,
  include_x = TRUE,
  include_y = TRUE,
  show_progress = TRUE,
  progress_every = 10,
  pdp_range = c(-0.5, 0.5),
  make_pdp = FALSE,
  mice_impute = TRUE,
  ymis_update = c("conditional", "marginal"),
  probit_prior = probit_prior_list(),
  save_y_pred = TRUE,
  save_z = TRUE,
  ...
)

missBART2(
  x,
  y,
  x_predict = NULL,
  n_reg_trees = 100,
  n_class_trees = 100,
  burn = 1000,
  iters = 1000,
  thin = 2,
  predict = TRUE,
  MH_sd = NULL,
  tree_prior_params = tree_list(...),
  hypers = hypers_list(...),
  scale = TRUE,
  include_x = TRUE,
  include_y = TRUE,
  show_progress = TRUE,
  progress_every = 10,
  pdp_range = c(-0.5, 0.5),
  make_pdp = FALSE,
  mice_impute = TRUE,
  ymis_update = c("conditional", "marginal"),
  save_y_pred = TRUE,
  save_z = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

numeric matrix (or data frame) of covariates. Missing covariate values are allowed in missBART2() and mvBART(), where they are handled inside the trees; missBART1() needs complete covariates.

y

numeric matrix (or vector) of responses, with NA for missing values.

x_predict

optional covariates at which to make out-of-sample predictions.

n_trees, n_reg_trees

number of trees in the BART model for the responses.

burn

number of burn-in iterations.

iters

number of posterior samples kept after burn-in and thinning.

thin

thinning interval. The sampler runs burn + thin * iters iterations.

predict

logical. Make predictions at x_predict?

tree_prior_params

tree prior and proposal settings, see tree_list().

hypers

hyperparameters of the BART model for the responses, see hypers_list().

scale

logical. Scale each response to [-0.5, 0.5] before fitting? missBART1() then also scales the covariates, so B_post refers to the scaled variables. Everything else is returned on the original scale.

include_x, include_y

logical. Use x and/or y as predictors of the missingness? include_y = FALSE assumes the responses are missing at random.

show_progress

logical. Print the iteration count?

progress_every

how often to update the iteration count.

pdp_range, make_pdp

for missBART2() with a univariate response: if make_pdp = TRUE, the latent missingness predictor is evaluated over a grid of (scaled) response values spanning pdp_range at every kept iteration and returned in pdp_out; apply stats::pnorm() to get the probability of being observed. Ignored by missBART1(), where the same curves follow directly from B_post.

mice_impute

logical. Initialise the missing responses with mice::mice()? Otherwise they start at the centre of the observed range.

ymis_update

how the Gaussian update of the missing responses treats rows that are only partly missing. "conditional" (the default) conditions on the observed responses in the same row. "marginal" draws from the corresponding margin of the full-row distribution, as written in Appendix C.1 of the paper and done by versions before 0.2.0. The two agree for univariate responses. Used by missBART1(), and by missBART2() when include_y = FALSE.

probit_prior

gamma prior settings for the precisions of the probit coefficients in missBART1(), see probit_prior_list().

save_y_pred

logical. Keep posterior predictive draws for the training data (y_pred)?

save_z

logical. Keep the draws of the latent probit variables (z_post)?

...

further arguments passed to tree_list() and hypers_list(). Arguments of earlier versions that are no longer used are ignored.

n_class_trees

number of trees in the probit BART model for the missingness indicators.

MH_sd

standard deviation of the random-walk proposal for missing responses in missBART2(). Defaults to 0.5 / ncol(y).

Value

An object of class "missBART": a list with, among others,

y_post

list of iters matrices with the BART mean function for each training row.

y_pred

list of posterior predictive draws for the training rows.

y_impute

list of vectors of imputed values, ordered as which(is.na(y)).

new_y_hat, new_y_post

lists with the mean function and posterior predictive draws at x_predict (or NA).

sigma_post

list of residual covariance matrices. omega_post is the same object under its old name.

B_post, R_post, tau_b

missBART1() only: probit coefficients, correlation matrices, and prior precisions of the coefficients.

var_imp

missBART2() only: matrix with the number of splitting rules on each predictor in the missingness trees, one row per kept iteration.

var_imp_reg

the same for the regression trees.

z_post

list of latent probit variables.

y_miss_accept

missBART2() only: Metropolis-Hastings acceptance rate for each missing value.

tree_accept

acceptance rates of the tree proposals.

Use fitted(), predict(), imputed_values(), completed_data(), coef() and varimp() to summarise a fit.

References

Goh, Y. C., Soh, W. K., Parnell, A. C. and Murphy, K. (2024). Joint models for handling non-ignorable missing data using Bayesian additive regression trees: application to leaf photosynthetic traits data. doi:10.48550/arXiv.2412.14946

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 200
x <- matrix(runif(n * 3), ncol = 3)
y_true <- cbind(sin(2 * pi * x[, 1]), x[, 2]^2) + matrix(rnorm(2 * n, sd = 0.2), ncol = 2)
# large values of the first response are more likely to be missing
y <- y_true
y[runif(n) < pnorm(2 * y_true[, 1] - 1), 1] <- NA

fit <- missBART1(x, y, n_trees = 20, burn = 100, iters = 100, thin = 1,
                 mice_impute = FALSE, show_progress = FALSE)
fit
#> missBART1 fit: 200 observations, 2 responses
#> Missing responses: 53 of 400 (13.2%)
#> Posterior samples: 100 (burn-in 100, thinning 1)
#> Tree acceptance rate: regression 0.14
head(imputed_values(fit))
#>   row column      mean        sd      lower    upper
#> 1   1     Y1 0.7951750 0.2789181 0.28832332 1.290783
#> 2   5     Y1 0.8680268 0.2504344 0.44719060 1.335738
#> 3  10     Y1 0.6088303 0.2555736 0.05654392 1.042045
#> 4  11     Y1 0.9759243 0.2448018 0.49286643 1.434412
#> 5  12     Y1 0.7663950 0.2482717 0.28646051 1.246861
#> 6  22     Y1 0.7867143 0.2395778 0.37375796 1.200557
coef(fit)
#> , , mean
#> 
#>                   Y1         Y2
#> Intercept  1.6870607  4.6919918

#>

fit2 <- missBART2(x, y, n_reg_trees = 20, n_class_trees = 10, burn = 100,
                  iters = 100, thin = 1, mice_impute = FALSE,
                  show_progress = FALSE)
varimp(fit2)
#>        X1        X2        X3        Y1        Y2 
#> 0.2614935 0.1336365 0.1178880 0.3044160 0.1825660
